Researching the economics of Africa's energy future

I study how African economies can grow while keeping energy secure and bringing emissions down, using modern econometric and data science methods.

Dr Dasauki MusaPostdoctoral Research Fellow, University of South Africa · Lecturer, Babcock University, Nigeria
Publications Ongoing research Contact me

News

Latest publications

    All publications

    Finding in focus

    21%

    Share of 43 African countries where the Environmental Kuznets Curve holds, meaning emissions eventually fall as incomes rise. In most countries, emissions keep rising with growth.

    Read the paper

    Research areas

    Energy markets and security

    Oil price shocks, energy security indices and how energy markets move stocks and economies.

    Climate and emissions

    The Environmental Kuznets Curve, climate policy uncertainty and the growth–emissions link in Africa.

    Green hydrogen and transition

    Techno-economic analysis of green hydrogen production and the economics of clean energy.

    Risk and financial markets

    Geopolitical risk, uncertainty spillovers, safe-haven assets and commodity volatility.

          Energy economist working on energy markets, energy security, climate change, clean and renewable energy, and green hydrogen.

          I hold a PhD in Energy Studies (Energy Economics) from the Centre for Petroleum, Energy Economics and Law (CPEEL), University of Ibadan. I have taught economics, econometrics, statistics and data science at Babcock University since 2017, and I am currently a Postdoctoral Research Fellow at the University of South Africa, working on a techno-economic analysis of green hydrogen production.

          Teaching and code

          Teaching and supervision

          I teach economics, econometrics, statistics and data science, and supervise projects and theses at BSc, PGD and MSc level. From 2023 to 2025 I coordinated the Economics Department's undergraduate programmes at Babcock University.

          Student research. I supervise students toward publication.

          • Emmanuel Enya (MSc): paper on global uncertainty and stock markets published in Cogent Economics & Finance (2026), co-supervised with Dr Uduakobong Edy-Ewoh.
          • Emmanuel Falayi (BSc): paper on climate-resilient tourism in East Africa accepted in the International Journal of Green Economics, after presenting it at DSA 2024 in London.

          Code and data

          Replication code and data are added to GitHub as each paper is published.
